chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Moalla ibn Muhammad, all together from Al-Washsha, who said:
I heard Al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man from the Children of Israel, whenever he intended to worship, would remain silent before that for ten years.'

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Reza (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ali al-Rida (AS)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of silence before worship in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) cites the practice of a man from the Children of Israel who observed silence for ten years before engaging in worship, illustrating the profound spiritual discipline required to purify the tongue. This narration, found in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *samt* (silence) not merely as absence of speech, but as an active, long-term preparation for divine connection and guarding against heedlessness.
